clue_text: Muhtaram Khanum Iskandari led the Society for the Patriotic Women of Iran until her death in July 1924; this woman took the chair after her.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The best-known women's-rights campaigner of the era, she is the first name anyone reaches for.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: She ran her own paper and her own school, not this society's chair.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: As Mozayyen al-Saltaneh she published a pioneering women's journal, so she fits the profile.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Her work was in publishing; this chair went to Afshar.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: She founded a women's association in the same decade.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Hers was a separate association in Shiraz; the Patriotic Women's chair was Afshar's.

explanation: The Society for the Patriotic Women of Iran was founded in 1922. Its first president, Muhtaram Khanum Iskandari, died in July 1924, and Masturah Afshar headed the society after her.
book_title: The State and the Subaltern: Modernization, Society and the State in Turkey and Iran
author: Touraj Atabaki (ed.)
chapter: Authority and Agency: Revisiting Women's Activism durin
supporting_passage: Founded in 1922, the Society had been headed by Masturah Afshar after the death of one of its founders and its first president, Muhtaram Khanum Iskandari (d. July 1924).

host_reactions.correct_generic: Masturah Afshar. She took the chair of the Society for the Patriotic Women of Iran in 1924, when death vacated it — the movement's oldest form of promotion.
host_reactions.wrong_generic: Wrong. A famous name in the cause is still the wrong name.

clue_text: Alongside equality before the law for Iran's male citizens and seats for religious minorities, the early constitutional enactments repealed this centuries-old poll tax on non-Muslims.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The other classic Islamic levy on non-Muslims, so the register sounds right.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The kharaj fell on land; the repeal was of the poll tax on non-Muslims themselves.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The Islamic tax a non-specialist reaches for first.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The zakat falls on Muslims' wealth, not on non-Muslims.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Another named religious levy, and it sounds like the same family.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The ushr was a tithe on produce; the poll tax repealed with the constitutional enactments was the jezyeh.

explanation: The early constitutional enactments granted equality before the law to male citizens, repealed the jezyeh — the poll tax levied on non-Muslims — and provided for some religious minorities to be represented in the majles.

clue_text: In the nationwide referendum held at the end of March 1979, this exact share of voters endorsed the establishment of an Islamic republic.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A big, believable landslide — the shape a rushed ballot usually takes.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The referendum was reported at 97 per cent, not a merely large majority.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: High enough to read as a mandate and still leave room for dissent.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The ballot was not close enough for a figure like this to be the recorded one.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The sort of qualified majority a genuinely contested vote produces.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The founding ballot of the Islamic republic was not contested at the box.

explanation: The referendum held at the end of March 1979 asked voters to approve the establishment of an Islamic republic, and the reported result was 97 per cent in favour.

author: Michael Axworthy

clue_text: On this date about 45,000 Iraqi ground troops crossed into Iran in four thrusts while Iraqi aircraft struck ten Iranian airbases, opening the war.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The date of the embassy seizure, and the one most often mixed up with the slide to war.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The invasion came almost a year later, in September 1980.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A turning-point date from the middle of the war, taught as the moment the tide turned.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: That is an Iranian push into Iraq, not the opening thrust into Iran.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The date the war stopped, easier to remember than the date it began.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: That is the ceasefire, eight years late for the first day.

explanation: On 22 September 1980, about 45,000 Iraqi ground troops entered Iran in four major thrusts while Iraqi aircraft struck ten Iranian airbases — the opening day of the eight-year war.
book_title: Revolutionary Iran: A History of the Islamic Republic
author: Michael Axworthy

host_reactions.correct_generic: 22 September 1980. Four major thrusts and ten airbases struck on the first day, and eight years of everything that followed.
